title: Revamp batch telemetry and introduce shadow-KV protection to reduce migration oscillation
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Background: Over the last 18 months we've accumulated multiple quick fixes to the continuous batching telemetry pipeline and ad-hoc KV cache guards introduced during hotfixes for model swap regressions. Symptoms include noisy per-batch metrics that obscure real latency regressions, repeated small migrations of session ownership (migration oscillation) when prefilling KV shards, and rare cases where newly warmed KV state causes 'shadow' reads that return stale embeddings during model checkpoints.

Goal: Cleanly separate telemetry emission from the batching fast path, formalize a shadow-KV protection contract to avoid cache shadowing during warmup/model swap, and add lightweight scheduler invariants to eliminate oscillatory slot reallocation. Deliverables are a refactor with measurable telemetry reduction, an API-level guard for shadow-KV write visibility, and a canary rollout plan with rollback gates.
acceptance_criteria: Batching hot path emits no blocking telemetry calls and end-to-end p99 generation latency impact < 1% in canary region
Drop in telemetry cardinality for per-batch metrics by >= 70% (observed in metrics_platform dashboard)
Shadow-KV protection prevents reads of entries marked 'warm-inflight' until checkpoint stable; verified by unit test + integration trace
Scheduler slot reassignments caused by prefetch priming are reduced to <1 per 10k sessions under synthetic load
Canary rollout completes with automatic rollback if increased 99th latency > 5% or error-rate > 0.5% above baseline
technical_notes: Introduce 'telemetry-emitter' worker pool: nonblocking, bounded queue, backpressure signals that are entirely decoupled from the batch commit path
Add header flag 'kv-visible-after' on prefills: write occurs to sharded-kv with staged visibility, coordinated by epoch heartbeat to avoid shadow reads
Scheduler invariant: owner-assignment must hold for min_hold_ms to reduce churn; implement token-bucket grace period rather than immediate requeue
Prefer async log/metric aggregation to external sink (metrics v2) with enforced sample rate config per metric name
Design avoids changing existing public RPCs; new behaviours are opt-in via feature flag 'kvcache-shadow-protect' and runtime-1.20 rollout table
rollout_plan: 2) Unit tests + integration tests in CI; e2e test harness with synthetic prefill traces
3) Canary deploy to us-west-2 single pool (5% traffic) for 48h; monitor latency, errors, and telemetry cardinality
4) Expand to us-east-1 (25% traffic) for 72h; run targeted regression prompts and embedding stability checks
5) Full roll to global runtime-1.20 when metrics stable for 7d; gradual ramp with automated rollback gates
test_plan: New unit tests for telemetry-emitter queue backpressure and drop behaviour
Integration test simulating model swap + concurrent prefill to validate 'kv-visible-after' semantics
Load test: 10k concurrent sessions with prefill skew to stress scheduler; assert reassignments < threshold
Chaos test: kill and restart one node during prefill; ensure no visible shadow reads and no session double-commit
Observability: create dashboard comparing old vs new per-batch metric cardinality and per-route p99 latencies

blockers: Metrics platform team needs a sampling config endpoint before we can flip high-cardinality metrics to sampled mode
Runtime sharding table migration schedule conflicts with planned dedicated pool maintenance on 2026-03-20
risks: If telemetry-emitter queue underruns, we may lose important microsecond-level diagnostic events; mitigated via sampled fallback path
Incorrect kv-visible-after semantics could block legitimate reads if epoch heartbeat delayed — risk reduced by conservative default visibility window
Scheduler min_hold_ms may increase steady-state slot utilization leading to slight throughput drop under very bursty loads
estimation_notes: Estimate 8 points: 3 for core refactor (emitter + queue), 2 for kv-visible-after contract and tests, 2 for scheduler invariant change and integration testing, 1 for rollout/observability dashboards.
